lines: Statim makes 68 decisions per second on a single GPU.
Laya needs a Python stack, but Statim runs on a 5.5 MB binary plus a gguf model file.
Statim runs Laya checkpoints and implements the Jev/Laya POST v1/systemone protocol so existing clients can switch by changing the base URL.
The state and all questions become one token sequence with a mask per option.
Type a department question and choice, get an answer like billing with 0.9948 probability.
On S1Bench, Statim 0.7.0 scores 0.638 macro above its untuned Laya base.
A rank-4 adapter uses 3.3 MB and adds 17 to 28 percent CPU latency.
You can list loaded models with GET v1 slash models.
Statim runs on Linux x86-64 with AVX2 and supports Vulkan on an RTX 3070.
Apache-2.0 licence allows any use, and Lev's authors tested it on S1Bench.
Copy the release URL, verify the checksums with sha256sum, then extract the tarball.
Save this for a Python user who wants to switch to a native C++ engine.
Native C++ replaces Python without losing accuracy.
